# Literal PBPS reflected Gibbs law and compact-observer mean

Authored analytic integration for Chen, Chewi, Lu and Zhang,
arXiv:2609.06905v1, Appendix C.1 reflected density and normalized mean.
The source-volume S_y is identified at EVERY y with the actual posterior
reflection, using genuine Gibbs integrability and exported affine normalization.

Tf closed-gradient membership, rough B.13, Gamma, invariance/nonexplosion,

/-- Literal every-y source reflection law and C1 mean, with normalization internal. -/
theorem reflected_gibbs_mean_c1
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    {V : E → ℝ} {α η : ℝ} (hα : 0 < α) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E, α*‖v‖^2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v)
    (hη : 0 < η) {f : E → ℝ} (hf : ContDiff ℝ 1 f) (hc : HasCompactSupport f) :
    let μ := (volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -V x)
    let R := fun y : E => μ.tilted (fun x => -‖x-y‖^2/(2*η))
    let S := fun y : E => (volume : Measure E).tilted
      (fun u => -V ((1/2:ℝ) • (y+u)) - ‖y-u‖^2/(8*η))
    (∀ y, S y = (R y).map (fun x : E => (2:ℝ) • x-y)) ∧
      ContDiff ℝ 1 (fun y : E => ∫ u, f u ∂S y)
 := by
  let μ := (volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -V x)
  let R := fun y : E => μ.tilted (fun x => -‖x-y‖^2/(2*η))
  let S := fun y : E => (volume : Measure E).tilted
    (fun u => -V ((1/2:ℝ) • (y+u)) - ‖y-u‖^2/(8*η))
  change (∀ y, S y = (R y).map (fun x : E => (2:ℝ) • x-y)) ∧
    ContDiff ℝ 1 (fun y : E => ∫ u, f u ∂S y)
  have hG := GibbsAugmentation.normalized_augmentation_density hα hV hH hη
  have hI : Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (-V x)) (volume : Measure E) :=
    Integrable.of_integral_ne_zero hG.1.ne'
  have : IsProbabilityMeasure μ := isProbabilityMeasure_tilted hI
  have hR (y : E) : R y = (volume : Measure E).tilted
      (fun x => -(V x + ‖x-y‖^2/(2*η))) := by
    dsimp only [R, μ]
    rw [tilted_tilted hI]
    congr 1
    funext x
    simp only [Pi.add_apply]
    ring
  have hS (y : E) : S y = (R y).map (fun x : E => (2:ℝ) • x-y) := by
    have hW (u : E) :
        V ((2:ℝ)⁻¹ • (u- -y)) + ‖(2:ℝ)⁻¹ • (u- -y)-y‖^2/(2*η) =
          V ((1/2:ℝ) • (y+u)) + ‖y-u‖^2/(8*η) := by
      have ha : (2:ℝ)⁻¹ • (u- -y) = (1/2:ℝ) • (y+u) := by
        simp [div_eq_mul_inv, sub_neg_eq_add, add_comm]
      have hb : (2:ℝ)⁻¹ • (u- -y)-y = (1/2:ℝ) • (u-y) := by
        norm_num
        module
      have hq : ‖(2:ℝ)⁻¹ • (u- -y)-y‖^2/(2*η) = ‖y-u‖^2/(8*η) := by
        rw [hb, norm_smul, norm_sub_rev u y]
        norm_num [Real.norm_eq_abs]
        field_simp
        ring
      rw [hq, ha]
    have haf := AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.AffineGibbs.map_affine_gibbs
      (fun x : E => V x + ‖x-y‖^2/(2*η)) (-y) (s := 2) (by norm_num)
    have hm : (fun x : E => -y+(2:ℝ) • x) = (fun x : E => (2:ℝ) • x-y) :=
      funext fun x => by abel
    rw [hm] at haf
    rw [hR]
    calc
      S y = (volume : Measure E).tilted (fun u =>
          -(V ((2:ℝ)⁻¹ • (u- -y)) + ‖(2:ℝ)⁻¹ • (u- -y)-y‖^2/(2*η))) := by
        dsimp only [S]
        congr 1
        funext u
        rw [hW]
        ring
      _ = _ := haf.symm
  refine ⟨hS, ?_⟩
  simp_rw [hS]
  exact AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.GaussianReflectedMean.gaussian_reflected_mean_c1
    μ hη hf hc

end
end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.ProximalBPS.LiteralReflectedMean

actual_complete_payload.statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space with its Borel measurable structure, including rank zero. Let V:E→ℝ be C2, α>0, and D²V(x)[v,v]≥α‖v‖² for all x,v. Let η>0 and let f:E→ℝ be C1 with compact support. Define μ=volume.tilted(−V), R_y=μ.tilted(x↦−‖x−y‖²/(2η)), and the literal source law S_y=volume.tilted(u↦−V((y+u)/2)−‖y−u‖²/(8η)). Then for EVERY y, S_y=(x↦2x−y)_#R_y, and the exact mean function y↦∫f(u)S_y(du) is C1. All actual Gibbs normalization, integrability, affine law and mean regularity ingredients are produced internally. This is attributed analytic integration for PBPS C.1, with explicitly broader sufficient background assumptions, not a standalone printed main theorem or rough B.13.

steps.title: Produce genuine Gibbs normalization before using a tilt
steps.text: Positive lower curvature and C2 V feed the existing Gibbs augmentation producer. Its actual positive partition integral is nonzero; Integrable.of_integral_ne_zero yields exp(−V)∈L1(volume). This establishes that the literal μ is a probability, rather than relying on a totalized zero integral. Finite-dimensional volume and its positive-open-set property are inherited ambient facts, not new theorem binders.

steps.title: Identify the actual posterior as the combined normalized potential
steps.text: Using the genuine exp(−V) integrability, the existing tilted_tilted theorem combines the literal μ tilt with its quadratic likelihood. Pointwise algebra gives the same combined potential V(x)+‖x−y‖²/(2η) at each y. No arbitrary almost-everywhere conditional representative is used.
steps.lean: hR; tilted_tilted hI; funext; Pi.add_apply; ring

steps.title: Keep the exact inverse map and the factor8η
steps.text: For T_y(x)=2x−y the inverse is (u+y)/2. Its displacement from y is (u−y)/2, so the original quadratic denominator2η becomes8η. This gives exactly the paper’s reflected source potential W_y. Its parameter-y score is −∇V((y+u)/2)/2−(y−u)/(4η); this differs from the u-gradient. The score formula is source context here, not an additional exported derivative theorem.
steps.lean: hW; ha; hb; hq; norm_smul; norm_sub_rev; exact rw [hq,ha]

steps.title: Apply the genuine normalized affine-map theorem
steps.text: The existing affine Gibbs theorem applies to F_y(x)=V(x)+‖x−y‖²/(2η), scale2 and translation−y. Its change-of-variables normalization retains the inverse Jacobian2^(−d), equivalently Z_S(y)=2^d Z_R(y), so the normalized laws agree exactly. Substitute the proved inverse-potential identity and rewrite −y+2x=2x−y. The result is every-y S_y=(T_y)_#R_y, including d=0.
steps.formula: d=\dim E,\quad |\det DT_y^{-1}|=2^{-d},\quad Z_S(y)=2^d Z_R(y),\quad S_y=(T_y)_\#R_y\qquad(\forall y).
steps.lean: AffineGibbs.map_affine_gibbs; haf; hm; hR; hW; hS

steps.title: Transport the whole literal mean function, then use true C1 regularity
steps.text: The Gaussian reflected-mean parent applies to the actual probability μ, η>0 and compact C1 f. Its domination, numerator derivative, positive normalizer and continuous integrated derivative are internal verified background. Rewrite the measure equality at EVERY y in the whole mean function and consume this C1 result. An AE fiber identity would not justify this derivative transport.
steps.formula: m(y)=\int f(u)S_y(du)=\int f(2x-y)R_y(dx)\quad(\forall y),\qquad m\in C^1(E).
steps.lean: refine ⟨hS,?_⟩; simp_rw [hS]; GaussianReflectedMean.gaussian_reflected_mean_c1 μ hη hf hc

steps.title: Consume the paper’s original kernel and a noncentered rank-zero source law
steps.text: The genuine Tests use the original two-sided Hessian and βη≤1 assumptions. MacroscopicEnergy supplies probability of the same μ; GaussianConditionalKernel constructs a Markov conditional R for the same Gaussian augmentation J and identifies every literal posterior fiber. The new law identity yields every source S_y probability and its smooth compact mean C1. Separately, dimension0 with V=0, α=η=1 and f=1 produces actual source mean1 and actual derivative0. Neither Test assumes centering or a closure certificate.
steps.formula: J=\operatorname{law}(X,X+\sqrt\eta G),\quad R\text{ is Markov and conditional for }J,\quad S_y=(2x-y)_\#R_y;\qquad d=0,\ V=0,\ f=1:\ m\equiv1,\ Dm\equiv0.
